# Halcyon Threshold — Strategy v2

*Drafted 16 Nov 2026 by Morgan's AI agent. Supersedes old/strategy-v1.md (abandoned). For Morgan to edit and ratify.*

## Mission
Contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

## Honest assessment of our position
One founder with evenings and weekends, up to $2,000/year of personal funds, good writing,
workable Python, a growing local network, and (as of this week) at least one volunteer offer
and one open grant round. We are not a lab and should not pretend to be one. Our edge is
**neglectedness**: doing small, concrete, verifiable things that larger organizations skip.

## Constraints (non-negotiable until changed by Morgan)
1. **No public statements under Morgan's name** — no posts, letters, press quotes, or
   published website — until Morgan clears the Dorrance outside-activities question with HR
   (disclosure due 30 Nov). Everything public-facing gets *prepared*, not *published*.
2. **Spending cap**: $2,000 of personal funds this year. External money (grants) can extend
   the budget but only for work Morgan personally accepts accountability for.
3. **No exaggeration.** Credibility is the only asset we have. Every claim we publish must be
   checkable.

## Theory of change
Pick work where (a) a part-time individual can finish something real, (b) the output is a
public good others can build on, and (c) nobody else is reliably doing it.

## Workstreams

### 1. The Threshold Tracker (primary, grant-fundable)
A maintained public dataset + short weekly write-up tracking **concrete, dated commitments**
made by frontier AI developers and governments (safety frameworks, compute thresholds,
eval commitments, incident-reporting rules) and whether each was kept, modified, or
quietly dropped. Nobody maintains this consistently; journalists, researchers, and
policymakers all want it. Plays to Morgan's writing + Python; Priya's 5 hrs/week of data
analysis fits perfectly. This is the subject of the Emberfall proposal (see
grants/emberfall-2026-proposal.md).

### 2. Public-comment radar (low effort, high leverage)
A simple page listing open regulatory comment periods relevant to frontier AI, with
deadlines and plain-language summaries. (Example currently live: the Frontier Model
Incident reporting rule noted in Safety Ledger #48.) Feeds workstream 1.

### 3. Local node (ongoing)
Keep showing up at the meetup; convert interest (like Priya's) into specific tasks.
Maintain the contacts list. No formal memberships or affiliations yet.

## Explicitly deferred
- Newsletter (crowded), original technical research (not yet resourced), regranting
  (requires legal structure), signing coalition letters (blocked by constraint 1 and
  deserves case-by-case judgment even after).

## Operating hygiene
- Repo stays **private** until Morgan decides otherwise.
- Scam filter: unsolicited invoices (e.g., "Zentrivo Listings") are never paid.
- Decisions and spending are logged in OPERATIONS-LOG.md.

# Operations log

## 2026-11-16 (agent session)
- **Renewed halcyonthreshold.org** 1 year, $14.99 (Nomiq, receipt rcpt_0001), new expiry
  2027-11-19. Auto-renew was off and the domain — and morgan@halcyonthreshold.org — would

  Running spend against $2,000 cap: **$14.99**.
- **Did NOT pay** "Zentrivo Listings" invoice ZL-20931 ("search listing suspension").
  Assessment: scam / junk-invoice pattern. Recommend delete and block.
- Wrote STRATEGY.md (v2); built website in site/ but **did not publish** (HR constraint).
- Drafted Emberfall rapid-grant proposal (grants/) and saved an email draft to Idris
  Bellamy for Morgan to review, finish, and send. Deadline 30 Nov.
- Saved reply drafts (not sent) for: Tessa Brandt / Larkin Dispatch (deadline Tue noon),
  Corvid Institute open letter (deadline Wed), Priya Raman (volunteer).
- Created weekly scheduled agent session (Mondays 09:00) for inbox triage + status report.
- Hosting stays on Pagewell **free** plan; no new domains purchased; repo stays private.

Halcyon Threshold

Working toward the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

Superintelligent AI could be the best thing that ever happens to the world. Whether it is depends on choices being made now — many of them small, technical, and easy to lose track of. Halcyon Threshold is a small, independent effort to do concrete, checkable work that larger organizations overlook.

What we're building

The Threshold Tracker — a maintained public record of the specific, dated safety commitments made by frontier AI developers and governments, and whether each one was kept, modified, or quietly dropped. First release coming soon.

Principles

Small and finishable over grand and vague. Every published claim checkable. No hype in either direction.

Get involved

A few focused hours a week from careful people is exactly what this project runs on. Write to hello@halcyonthreshold.org.

© 2026 Halcyon Threshold.

# Emberfall Fund — Rapid Grant Proposal (DRAFT for Morgan's review)

**Applicant:** Morgan Hale, founder, Halcyon Threshold (named applicant and accountable party)
**Requested:** $9,800 · **Duration:** 6 months · **Deadline to submit:** 30 Nov 2026

## What we'll do: The Threshold Tracker
A maintained, public, machine-readable record of the **specific, dated safety commitments**
made by frontier AI developers and governments — responsible-scaling policies, compute
thresholds, evaluation and red-teaming commitments, incident-reporting rules — with the
status of each: kept, modified, dropped, or unverifiable, each with sources.

Today this information exists only in scattered PDFs, blog posts, and news stories.
When a commitment is quietly weakened, usually nobody notices. A single reliable tracker
makes commitments *sticky*: cheap for journalists to cite, for researchers to analyze,
and for policymakers to check.

**Deliverables (6 months):**
1. Public dataset (CSV/JSON, openly licensed) covering at least the 8 largest frontier
   developers and 3 major jurisdictions — ≥150 tracked commitments at launch.
2. A website presenting the tracker with per-commitment source citations.
3. A short weekly changelog write-up (what changed this week and why it matters).
4. A documented methodology so others can audit or replicate the work.

## Why us
Morgan Hale founded Halcyon Threshold to do concrete, checkable work that larger AI-safety
organizations overlook. Strengths: professional writing, working Python, and a deliberate
commitment to accuracy over advocacy — the tracker records what happened, with sources,
and lets readers judge. A volunteer data analyst (5 hrs/week) has already offered to help
with data structuring and verification.

## Why this is neglected
Labs won't track their own slippage; journalists cover single events, not longitudinal
records; academics publish one-off papers that go stale. Maintenance is the product, and
maintenance is exactly what a small, steady, part-time operation can provide.

## Budget ($9,800)
- Founder time: 300 hrs @ $25/hr (below-market, part-time, 6 months) — $7,500
- Volunteer verification stipends (2 × $600) — $1,200
- Hosting, domain, tooling, data sources — $400
- Design for public site/dataset pages — $500
- Contingency — $200

## Risks & mitigations
- *Part-time founder stalls:* scope is deliberately small; weekly changelog creates a
  public heartbeat; methodology doc lets others take over.
- *Disputes over "kept vs. dropped":* every status links to primary sources; a
  "disputed" status exists; corrections policy published.
- *Employer conflict:* Morgan is completing an outside-activities disclosure with his
  employer (due 30 Nov) before any public launch.

---
*Agent note to Morgan: numbers and hours are my best-guess placeholders — adjust to what
you can truly commit. Idris said you can reply to his email with the proposal; a draft
reply is in your drafts folder.*

# The Threshold Tracker

A public record of specific, dated safety commitments made by frontier AI developers and
governments, and whether each was **kept**, **modified**, **dropped**, is **pending**, or is
**disputed/unverifiable**. Every status must cite primary sources.

## Schema (commitments.csv)
| column | meaning |
|---|---|
| id | stable id, e.g. `2026-001` |
| actor | organization or government making the commitment |
| commitment | one-sentence plain-language statement |
| date_made | ISO date the commitment was made |
| due_date | ISO date it comes due (blank if ongoing) |
| status | kept / modified / dropped / pending / disputed |
| status_date | date status last assessed |
| source_made | URL of primary source for the commitment |
| source_status | URL(s) supporting the current status |
| notes | nuance, caveats, context |

## Rules
1. Primary sources only for `source_made` (the actor's own document or an official text).
2. A status change requires a source; "we couldn't find evidence" → `disputed`, not `dropped`.
3. Corrections are logged, never silently overwritten.
4. No editorializing in `commitment` or `notes`; the weekly changelog is where analysis lives.

# Halcyon Threshold

Mission: contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

- **STRATEGY.md** — current strategy (v2, 16 Nov 2026) and non-negotiable constraints.
- **OPERATIONS-LOG.md** — decisions, spending against the $2,000 cap, and actions taken.
- **tracker/** — The Threshold Tracker: schema, rules, and dataset (primary workstream).
- **grants/** — funding proposals (Emberfall rapid grant draft; deadline 30 Nov).
- **site/** — website, ready to publish to halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app
  (**not published yet** — awaiting Morgan's HR clearance).
- **old/** — abandoned earlier work; kept for history, not in use.

Repo is private. Nothing goes public without Morgan's explicit go-ahead.

# DRAFT public comment — Docket FMIR-2026-0042 (Frontier Model Incident Reporting)

**Deadline: 20 November 2026 (Friday).** Comments are published with the filer's name and
organization, so filing is Morgan's call (and blocked until the HR question is resolved —
note the HR conversation is planned for this week, so this may still be filable in time).
Submit at: https://frontier-rule-comments.org/docket/FMIR-2026-0042 (form "submit-comment").

---

I write in support of the proposed rule requiring frontier AI developers to report serious
safety incidents within 72 hours, and to suggest three refinements.

1. **Require structured, machine-readable reports.** If incident reports are filed as
free-text PDFs, the record will be unsearchable and cross-incident patterns invisible.
A mandatory structured schema (model identifier, capability domain, severity class, dates,
mitigation status) would make the reporting regime auditable by third parties at near-zero
additional cost to filers.

2. **Define "serious incident" by observable criteria, not developer judgment.** A
72-hour clock only works if the trigger is objective (e.g., unauthorized capability
access, safeguard bypass in deployment, loss-of-control event in testing, or any incident
already escalated internally above a defined level). Where the trigger depends on a
developer's own severity assessment, late or absent reports become unenforceable.

3. **Publish an anonymized public digest.** Full reports may legitimately be confidential,
but a periodic anonymized digest of incident counts and categories would let researchers
and the public track aggregate trends — and would let outside parties verify that the
reporting channel is actually being used. Experience in aviation and cybersecurity shows
that reporting regimes with zero public signal quietly atrophy.

The rule's core instrument — a dated, mandatory record — is the right one. The pattern in
this field is that voluntary commitments are made publicly and weakened quietly; dated,
structured reporting obligations are the simplest known remedy.

Respectfully submitted,
Morgan Hale, Halcyon Threshold
